name: AI4Shipwrecks
description:
A dataset for AI for shipwreck detection from side scan sonar imagery featuring sonar imagery and labels for 28 sites surveyed from an underwater robotics platform. A cross disciplinary asset for history, environmental science and AI classrooms.

This dataset was selected from community submissions to Dear Colleague Letter NSF 25-018 to facilitate AI education and researcher skill development.

name: Cell Painting Gallery
description:
Microscopy images of billions of cells responding to drugs and genetic changes and their corresponding profiles. Enables AI learning to discover connections between genes and diseases and to find new medicines.

This dataset was selected from community submissions to Dear Colleague Letter NSF 25-018 to facilitate AI education and researcher skill development.

name: DoD Responsible AI (RAI) Toolkit
description: The RAI Toolkit is a collection of guidance, processes, and resources to aid in RAI development. This includes the interactive SHIELD assessment tool, as well as a large tools list. This is supported by the Department of Defense Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office (CDAO).

name: DOE ALCF AI training program
description: DOE’s Argonne Leadership Computing Facility (ALCF) offers video lectures and hands-on activities on introductory and advanced topics in AI for Science on supercomputers. The courses are targeted for undergraduate and graduate students at U.S. universities and community colleges interested in learning foundational concepts of AI and its applications to science. Basic experience with Python is needed but supercomputing or AI knowledge is not required.

name: DOE INCITE
description: DOE invites proposals to access its leadership high performance computing systems at Argonne and Oak Ridge National Laboratories through its INCITE program at doeleadershipcomputing.org. The current call for proposals closes June 14, 2024.

name: FathomNet Database
description:
The FathomNet Database can be used to train, test, and validate state-of-the-art AI algorithms to help us understand our ocean and its inhabitants. Leveraging imagery from a network of global contributors, this open-source, publicly available database provides tools and services for a wide spectrum of users, from marine biologists and data scientists to graduate students and ocean enthusiasts. FathomNet Database is integrated with the FathomNet Portal and can be linked to a number of external services via an API. Labeled imagery from the database is also used in an innovative community science mobile game, FathomVerse.

This dataset was selected from community submissions to Dear Colleague Letter NSF 25-018 to facilitate AI education and researcher skill development.

name: Johns Hopkins Turbulence Database
description:
Over one petabyte (1,000 terabytes) of turbulent flow simulation data created from high-fidelity numerical simulations of the Navier-Stokes equations. Solution fields such as velocity and pressure can be queried at any desired positions and times in the flow using virtual sensors, removing the need for researchers to have access to large computational resources.

This dataset was selected from community submissions to Dear Colleague Letter NSF 25-018 to facilitate AI education and researcher skill development.

name: March of Dimes Microbiome Preterm Birth DREAM Challenge dataset
provider: Dimes Prematurity Research Center at UCSF
description:
A dataset of the vaginal microbiome, consisting of over 3,500 samples from more than 1,200 pregnant individuals, that was used in a crowdsourced machine learning challenge for the prediction of preterm birth. A publication regarding this work https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/38134931, and a visualization tool for this data, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39345789.

This dataset was selected from community submissions to Dear Colleague Letter NSF 25-018 to facilitate AI education and researcher skill development.

links.title: March of Dimes Data Repository for Preterm Birth Research

name: NASA Earth Science AI Training Datasets
description: This repository contains several NASA Earth Science AI training datasets, including synthetic aperture radar (SAR) raster imagery for various flood events in the United States and Bangladesh, tropical storm wind speed data from the Atlantic and East Pacific Oceans from 2000 to 2019, Marine debris detection on ocean surface, and field boundary segmentation for Rwanda.

name: NASA Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLS) Foundation Model
description: HLS FM is a geospatial foundation model created in partnership with IBM using NASA’s Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLS) dataset available on Hugging Face. Source code is available on GitHub. See also the publication, 2023 Summer school training material on using the HL FM, and a Youtube video on HLS FM.

name: NASA HLS Burn Scars training dataset
description: AI training dataset for satellite image-based burn scar detection.

name: NASA Multi-temporal crop classification training dataset
description: AI training dataset for satellite image-based multi-temporal crop classification.

name: NASA Science Ethical AI Resources
description: A set of principles and best practices for applying AI within scientific research and applications, built in partnership with the American Geophysical Union (AGU).

links.title: Report on Ethical and Responsible Use of AI/ML in the Earth, Space, and Environmental Sciences
NASA’s Ethical AI checklist to its community

name: NASA Science Large Language Models
description: Created in collaboration with IBM, this specialized language model trained on scientific corpus collected from relevant publications (NASA ADS, AGU, AMS, PubMed). The initial version and a sentence-transformer model built upon this domain-adapted encoder are accessible on Hugging Face.

name: NASA Science Mission Directorate Curated AI training sets
description: This repository of AI training datasets resides on AWS and includes datasets from all science divisions

name: NIH All of Us Researcher Workbench
description: The All of Us Researcher Workbench is a secure platform that provides comprehensive health information of more than 500,000 people, including whole genome sequences, electronic health records, surveys, wearable data and more. It includes demo notebooks for machine learning and other AI techniques.

name: NIH ImmPort
description: ImmPort from NIAID is a publicly accessible data sharing platform supporting immunology research and clinical studies. ImmPort offers curated datasets and reference datasets that adhere to the FAIR Principles and is certified by CoreTrustSeal.

name: NIH Medical Imaging and Data Resource Center (MIDRC)
description: MIDRC is a curated, open medical imaging data repository and commons to enable AI algorithm development. MIDRC is also available via the NCATS N3C secure data enclave (see N3C). Open MIDRC data with de-identified medical imaging data available directly via the link.

name: NIH National Clinical Cohort Collaborative (N3C)
description:
N3C Clinical is a centralized clinical data repository and analysis hub containing the nation’s largest open-science resource of real-world data (RWD), created in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The repository contains multi-modal datasets including de-identified clinical data linked to CMS Medicare and Medicaid claims data, national mortality data, imaging data, and viral genome sequences. Over 80 healthcare systems have provided EHR data to the enclave, enabling research projects resulting in over 120 peer-reviewed publications.

This infrastructure has since been repurposed to enable unprecedented cross-institution collaboration and sharing of research best practices on major diseases such as cancer and renal disease.

N3C is funded by the National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences (NCATS), an institute of the NIH, as a public-private-government partnership. Researchers who apply to participate in N3C can gain access to the following resources:

  • Over 33 billion rows of de-identified EHR records representing over 22 million individuals linked through privacy preserving record linkage. This clinical data is harmonized and transformed into the OMOP common data model
  • Over 60 public datasets are available to integrate into analysis, including U.S. Census data, pollution index, Rural-Urban Commuting Area Codes (RUCA), etc.
  • Over 2,000 community-maintained OMOP concept sets as well as a library of reusable knowledge objects of cohort definitions, variables and, clinical analysis templates • Access to the Palantir Foundry platform powering N3C inclusive of autoscaling analytical compute (CPU + GPU)
  • Data science education and training material available as well as synthetic datasets that can be used for active learning exercises

Access Process

Access to N3C resources requires registration on one of two tracks:

  • Research Track – Access to clinical data resources requires either affiliation with a research institution which has executed a data use agreement with the NIH or submission of an individual DUA as a citizen scientist. Once this is executed, a project proposal can be submitted within the platform for a specific level of data obfuscation appropriate for your research. Information and registration instructions can be found at https://covid.clinicalcohort.org/for-researchers/
  • Education Track – Real-world data and data science educational material, including access to representative synthetic datasets. Access requirements and registration instructions are available at https://education.clinicalcohort.org/

name: NIH Science Collaborative for Health disparities and Artificial intelligence Reduction of Errors  (SCHARE)
description:
SCHARE is a cloud-based population science data platform designed to accelerate population health research, including chronic diseases, health disparities & health outcomes by utilizing transparent artificial intelligence (AI) approaches with a focus on the reduction of errors in the use and reuse of models designed to accelerate innovative research that includes place-based factors and biologics for whole-person health discoveries.

SCHARE aims to fill five critical gaps:

  • Leverage population science, place-based, and behavioral Big Data and cloud computing tools to foster a paradigm shift in health disparity and healthcare delivery outcomes research to generate innovative whole-person health discoveries, especially in chronic diseases
  • Advance use of transparency and sophisticated inquiry to develop innovative strategies and differing perspectives to foster reproducibility and to reduce AI errors
  • Upskill novice untrained users in data science through cloud computing skills training, cross-discipline mentoring, and multi-career level collaborating on research
  • Provide a data science cloud computing and data center resource for community colleges and low resource institutions and organizations
  • Offer a project data repository centered on core common data elements for enhanced data interoperability and compliance with NIH Data Management and Sharing Policy

THINK A THONS

Monthly webinars designed to upskill novice untrained users in data science and cloud computing in order to foster a research paradigm shift to use of Big Data in population health to accelerate innovative research. Topics prepare novice users to adopt cloud computing analytics, to prepare and use big data, and to learn how to be transparent in using AI for reproducibility and reduction of errors. Attendees are multi-career level from students to senior investigators, multi-discipline from data scientist to varied fields of research. This generational career and discipline exchange enables mentoring and coaching up and down the levels of experience. In addition, research think-a-thons are launched to provide participants hands-on experiences using cloud computing, enables learning across disciplines, and results in a publication.

name: NOAA Open Data Dissemination
description: The NOAA Open Data Dissemination program includes hundreds of NOAA datasets for earth systems and AI/ML applications; updated on a quarterly basis. The datasets are organized by the NOAA Line Office and programmatic area that generated the original dataset.

name: NOAA Tropical Cyclone Precipitation, Infrared, Microwave, and Environmental Dataset
description: TC PRIMED is a dataset that is suitable for multiple AI/ML applications centered around passive microwave observations of global tropical cyclones from low-Earth-orbiting satellites. Jupyter Notebooks are available for AI developers at: github.com/noaa-ncai/learning-journey/tree/main/tcprimed

name: OpenTopography Digital Elevation Model Data
description:
OpenTopography facilitates efficient access to topography data, tools, and resources to advance our understanding of the Earth’s surface, vegetation, and built environment.

This data collection includes nearly 300 open-access, digital elevation model datasets, primarily meter-scale data derived from lidar, covering the US and several international locations. Additional topography data, including high-resolution (better than 1m/pixel) lidar point cloud datasets, are available via the OpenTopography science gateway. OpenTopography hosts and distributes topographic datasets from around the world along with web based user-friendly processing tools for research and public use.

OpenTopography is jointly operated by the San Diego Supercomputer Center at UC San Diego, the EarthScope Consortium, and Arizona State University’s School of Earth and Space Exploration and is funded by the National Science Foundation’s Division of Earth Sciences. More information at opentopography.org.

This dataset was selected from community submissions to Dear Colleague Letter NSF 25-018 to facilitate AI education and researcher skill development.

name: PatchDB
description:
A dataset of approximately 36,000 real-world software patches, including 12,000 security-related examples. Ideal for cybersecurity education and training in automated vulnerability detection.

This dataset was selected from community submissions to Dear Colleague Letter NSF 25-018 to facilitate AI education and researcher skill development.

name: Phase-Field Brittle Fracture Simulation
description:
A dataset of 1,000 high-fidelity phase-field fracture simulations under varying loading and unloading conditions, represented as boundary constraints. The simulations capture multiple complex crack growth and propagation in hyperelastic materials, providing a rich resource for model development, validation, and benchmarking.

This dataset was selected from community submissions to Dear Colleague Letter NSF 25-018 to facilitate AI education and researcher skill development.

name: SecureChain
description:
Development of a unified knowledge graph to continually collect and track software dependency and vulnerabilities discussed in various online documents.

This dataset was selected from community submissions to Dear Colleague Letter NSF 25-018 to facilitate AI education and researcher skill development.

name: UCSF Industry Documents Library
description:
The UCSF Industry Documents Library (IDL) is a digital repository of over 24 million documents publicly released from industries which impact public health. Hosted by the UCSF Library since 2002, the IDL has been cited by researchers in more than 1,200 publications including peer-reviewed research, government reports, journalism, and educational resources. Data can be downloaded through a free API or as prepackaged datasets which include OCR text and detailed metadata.

This dataset was selected from community submissions to Dear Colleague Letter NSF 25-018 to facilitate AI education and researcher skill development.

name: USDA Census of Agriculture
description: The Census of Agriculture is a complete survey of U.S. farms and ranches conducted every five years by USDA’s National Agricultural Statistics Service. It covers land use and ownership, operator characteristics, production practices, income and expenditures, and more. Quick Stats allows searchable access to the 6 million data points in the 2022 census (released February 2024) and other NASS data products. Downloadable compressed files are also available.

name: USGS Autonomously Collected Benthic Imagery for Substrate Prediction, Lake Michigan 2020-2021
description: These data consist of down-looking images of Lake Michigan benthos, collected in 2020 and 2021 with an autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV). Information about each image (i.e., latitude, longitude, depth from surface, altitude, roll, pitch, yaw, and creation time) can be found in the associated csv file. Substrate type was divided into 9 classes based on the Coastal and Marine Ecological Classification Standard (CMECS) and each image was assigned a substrate class by at least 3 trained labelers.

name: USGS GeoNatShapes: a natural feature reference dataset for mapping and AI training
description: These data were compiled for the use of training natural feature machine learning (GeoAI) detection and delineation. The natural feature classes include the Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) feature types Basins, Bays, Bends, Craters, Gaps, Guts, Islands, Lakes, Ridges and Valleys, and are an aerial representation of those GNIS point features. Features were produced using heads-up digitizing from 2018 to 2019 by Dr. Sam Arundel's team at the U.S. Geological Survey, Center of Excellence for Geospatial Information Science, Rolla, Missouri, USA, and Dr. Wenwen Li's team in the School of Geographical Sciences at Arizona State University, Tempe, Arizona, USA.

name: USGS Spot Elevations Training Dataset
description: These image/label pairs were created to add to larger benchmark text datasets to enable the detection and recognition of spot elevation on historical topographic maps in the U.S. (HTMC). The pairs were created by manually heads-up digitizing bounding boxes around the 350 spot elevations in whole and one around each of the individual characters in the spot elevation. These rectangles were used to request images from the HTMC service at https://services.arcgisonline.com/arcgis/rest/services/USA_Topo_Maps/MapServer, and automatically create the accompanying label.

name: USGS The National Map Data Download and Visualization Services
description:
The National Geospatial Program (NGP) is contributing essential data holdings through The National Map (TNM). TNM offers a comprehensive range of topographic information vital for various applications. These resources encompass topographic maps and geographic information system (GIS) data covering a wide array of geographic features and attributes crucial for research, education, and decision-making processes.
The data include detailed information on elevation, hydrography, watersheds, geographic names, orthoimagery, governmental units/boundaries, transportation networks, and land cover. This wealth of data serves as a foundational resource for understanding the landscape and environment of the nation, facilitating analysis, visualization, and modeling across different disciplines.

name: USGS Training and validation data from the AI for Critical Mineral Assessment Competition
description: Extracting useful and accurate information from scanned geologic and other earth science maps is a time-consuming and laborious process involving manual human effort. To address this limitation, the USGS partnered with the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) to run the AI for Critical Mineral Assessment Competition, soliciting innovative solutions for automatically georeferencing and extracting features from maps. The competition opened for registration in August 2022 and concluded in December 2022. Training and validation data from the competition are provided here, as well as competition details and baseline solutions. The data are derived from published sources and are provided to the public to support continued development of automated georeferencing and feature extraction tools. References for all maps are included with the data.

name: USGS Water Use Estimates
description:
The USGS collaborates with local, state, and federal partners to gather and incorporate water-use data with other datasets covering climate, population, geography, system characteristics, land use, social factors, and economics. This information is then integrated into a modeling framework to generate national estimates of water withdrawal and consumption (evapotranspiration of withdrawn water) from both groundwater and surface-water sources. These estimates are crucial for understanding how water is used and for assessing the balance between water supply and demand. Withdrawals for public supply water use, and withdrawals and consumptive use for irrigation water use are estimated for each month of the period 2000-2020 for all watersheds at the 12-digit hydrologic unit code level (HUC-12) in the conterminous United States. The withdrawal and consumptive use estimates for thermoelectric power water use are available for each month of the period from 2008-2020, by power plant. The models provide estimates at finer temporal and spatial resolution than previous annual, county-level estimates published by the USGS.

See https://www.usgs.gov/mission-areas/water-resources/science/water-use-united-states#overview for details.

name: USPTO Bulk Datasets
description: USPTO patents and trademarks offer a rich dataset of complex language, covering a wide range of technical topics in a structured format. This page provides a single repository for obtaining raw-bulk download patent and trademarks publications and grants for use in the development of robust language models.

name: USPTO Research Datasets
description: This page hosts a collection of patent and trademark datasets related to intellectual property, entrepreneurship and innovation topics. The datasets and corresponding supplementary documentation is specifically formatted to aid academic researchers.
